shipped.title: Prevent repeat RSVPs for already-answered Guests
shipped.summary: The RSVP flow resolves append-only history latest-wins by guest_id, shows completed Parties a confirmed already-received state, limits partial Parties to unanswered Guests, and rechecks live state server-side before appending; the short completed state also fills the repeating PatternWall through the footer.
shipped.notes: Implementation identified at commit 82e0f93. The RSVP flow resolves append-only history latest-wins by guest_id, shows completed Parties a confirmed already-received state, limits partial Parties to unanswered Guests, and rechecks live state server-side before appending; the short completed state fills PatternWall through the footer. 142/142 tests pass; lint and TypeScript are clean. content-fidelity and design-reviewer PASS verdicts, plus verification, are recorded in step_log. No deployment is represented by this record.

defects_discovered.summary: The short already-received RSVP state ended its invitation-pattern background above the footer instead of filling the remaining page height like Home.
defects_discovered.root_cause: PatternWall sized only to its content: the body’s flexible main element was not a flex column and the wall itself did not grow into main’s remaining height.
defects_discovered.fix: Made main a flex column and PatternWall flex-grow through the remaining height, preserving the shared repeating tile treatment and natural sizing on long Pages.

defects_discovered.summary: An eligible Guest’s +1 controls were hidden in the initial unanswered RSVP state and appeared only after an attending answer, instead of appearing immediately after the primary Guest’s RSVP section.
defects_discovered.root_cause: The +1 renderer required at least one attending answer and sat after the complete Party member map, so the unanswered state suppressed the controls and could not place them after the primary Guest.
defects_discovered.fix: Acceptance repair under issue 019f4043-aa8e at commit 27f2018: show the +1 section before attendance is answered, render it immediately after the primary Guest, and hide it only when every displayed Party member declines.

defects_discovered.summary: The local Next.js development server redirected its HTTP RSVP URL to unavailable HTTPS and set HSTS, making the local preview unreachable in a browser.
defects_discovered.root_cause: The production HTTPS/HSTS middleware policy also applied to Next.js development requests, whose forwarded protocol is HTTP even though the local server has no HTTPS listener.
defects_discovered.fix: Acceptance repair under issue 019eebbd-bce2 at commit 27f2018: exempt development and local hostnames from the HTTPS redirect and HSTS while preserving both protections outside local development.

decisions.title: The site-wide rollout's wall mechanism is superseded by the shared cached image
decisions.summary: Issue 019f3fd3-f977 (site-wide pattern rollout) inherits the accepted 35%-over-cream treatment verbatim, but its wall mechanism — the separately-baked public/pattern/wall-tile.webp — is superseded by issue 019f406a-a40a (Home wall sources the gate's cached full-color image): the wall becomes one shared full-color image muted via CSS over token cream, browser-cached from the gate. The rollout depends on 019f406a-a40a landing first; f977's depends_on carries 019f406a-a40a. The shared-image approach also resolves the recorded advisory that wall-tile.webp bakes the literal cream #ECDFD1.

decisions.title: +1 names logged to an additive plus_one_names reference sheet
decisions.summary: When a Guest names a plus-one at RSVP, the +1's name is additionally appended to a new plus_one_names tab in the same spreadsheet — a flat, human-readable reference log for the couple's off-website planning. The append is best-effort and non-blocking (a failure logs server-side and never fails the RSVP) and deduped per distinct +1 per party by gating on a newly-minted +1 id (resolution.isNew). The official-guest-list write-back (ADR 019eebb3-f8db) and the rsvps recording are unchanged — the Team Lead's ruling is that main-sheet recording stays as is. It is its own slice (019f407a-eb9a-7d11-8355-92727795951f) with its own ADR, drafted by the architect and alignment-gated.

decisions.title: +1 becomes an explicit toggle with required name
decisions.summary: For issue 019f4043-bf72: an attending Guest with plus_one_allowed gets an explicit 'bringing a guest' choice; the +1 name is required only when bringing, and declining writes no +1 data (the server already emits a +1 row only on a non-empty name). This composes with 019f4043-aa8e, which hides all +1 controls when the Guest is not attending.

decisions.title: The Name gate wears a distinct full-color invitation treatment, not the muted wall
decisions.summary: The Name gate page carries the FULL-COLOR invitation pattern as its background — distinct from the accepted 35%-over-cream muted wall used on every other guest Page — with the name-entry form on a solid token-cream panel. The gate is text-light, so full color behind a panel conforms to the no-text-over-pattern rule. This is the Team Lead's Sprint-4 ruling, shipped as 019f406a-799c.

decisions.title: The pattern is applied through a shared PatternWall leaf component; gate and admin excluded by default
decisions.summary: The pattern treatment reaches every guest Page through PatternWall, a single shared leaf component (per the Swappable-leaf-components philosophy), so changing the treatment is a one-component edit rather than a per-page change. The Name gate and the admin area are excluded from PatternWall by default — the gate carries its own full-color treatment and admin stays plain. Recorded in ADR 019f4098-922e-7ce5-bca9-15666b897869.

decisions.title: One cached tile-full.webp sources the gate and every guest page
decisions.summary: A single image file, public/pattern/tile-full.webp, now sources both the gate background and the wall on every guest Page. Because the gate is every guest's first page, that image is already browser-cached when they reach the rest of the site; the wall is muted from the same file via CSS over token cream rather than a separately-baked tile, and the old wall-tile.webp was removed. This is a browser-cache performance property of the shared image, not a per-page asset.

retrospective_notes.title: RSVP form carries four non-blocking a11y-polish advisories worth a future accessibility slice
retrospective_notes.body: The RSVP +1 feature (shipped Sprint 4, merge 002de90) passed design-reviewer with 0 blocking findings and 4 non-blocking a11y-polish advisories on the form: (1) focus is not moved to the invalid name field on a submit-empty validation error; (2) the success-card swap relies on aria-live rather than a focus move; (3) the name placeholder uses the default color, not a token; (4) the error node is both role=alert and an aria-describedby target, a minor double-read. Focus management on validation error and on success is the common throughline. The Team Lead's assessment on ship: these are polish worth a future accessibility slice. No issue was filed.

retrospective_notes.title: The rollout's design review caught body-adjacent text floating on the pattern — the panel discipline held
retrospective_notes.body: The site-wide pattern rollout (019f3fd3-f977) FAILed design-reviewer on one blocker: the Travel page's .sectionHeading labels floated directly on the pattern instead of sitting on a surface. The prescribed surface-chip landed and re-verified PASS. The no-text-over-pattern panel discipline held across the rollout because the gate flagged the single place a label had escaped a panel — FAIL, chip, PASS.

retrospective_notes.title: One chartered ADR has a recorded alignment pass; the PatternWall ADR does not
retrospective_notes.body: The plus_one_names reference-sheet ADR (019f4079-fa3a) has an alignment_review_pass in step_log. The shared PatternWall ADR (019f4098-922e) is a chartered persistent-doc artifact referenced by the sprint decisions, but the authoritative on-disk step_log contains no alignment verdict for it; Sprint 4 therefore does not represent that ADR as alignment-passed.

retrospective_notes.title: A shell cwd drifted into a worktree and an initial merge ran from the wrong branch
retrospective_notes.body: During integration a shell's working directory drifted into a per-slice git worktree, and an initial merge was attempted from the wrong branch; the tell was an 'Already up to date' result that did not match what the merge should have done. Running `git branch --show-current` revealed the drift, and the merge was redone from the correct branch. The mismatch between the expected merge and the 'Already up to date' output is what exposed the wrong-branch state.

retrospective_notes.title: The close gates caught Git-to-sprint and ADR-gate source-of-truth mismatches before merge
retrospective_notes.body: The first Sprint-4 close/merge review FAILed because sprint_4 was active and uncommitted while its shipped list included the repeat-RSVP implementation before that implementation had a commit. Reconciliation against Git tied the +1/local-development acceptance repairs to 27f2018 and the repeat-RSVP implementation to 82e0f93; every shipped entry now identifies committed implementation and the archive contains nine closed Sprint-4 issue records. The second close-gate cycle confirmed that reconciliation and FAILed on the missing alignment verdict for ADR 019f4098-922e; under the two-FAIL escalation rule, Sprint 4 is BLOCKED and merge is prohibited.
